name: exact_title_no_authors
why: Both sides bare: an identical title clears even the raised no-author bar of 90.

name: exact_title_same_author
why: Identical title and author - the author boost is capped at 100.

name: author_initials_and_suffix_punctuation
why: 'L.E. Modesitt Jr.' and 'L. E. Modesitt, Jr.' are the same person once periods and commas are stripped, so the author gate passes and boosts.

name: author_surname_first
why: 'Butcher, Jim' vs 'Jim Butcher' - token_set_ratio after comma stripping.

name: leading_article_stripped_from_title
why: 'The Hobbit' and 'Hobbit' normalize to the same string.

name: same_series_same_index
why: Series names agree and both indexes are 2 - nothing rejects it.

name: series_index_string_forms_compare_equal
why: Indexes reach the matcher as whatever the metadata held - '01' and '1.0' are the same book, so parsing stays tolerant even though the comparison is now numeric.

name: unparseable_series_index_is_missing_metadata
why: An index that is not a number ('II') is absent metadata, not evidence of a different book - it must not reject an otherwise perfect match.

name: same_series_but_only_one_side_has_an_index
why: A series name on both sides with an index on only one is still missing metadata - the numeric comparison only rejects when both sides give a number.

name: series_name_with_leading_article
why: 'The Dresden Files' vs 'Dresden Files' compare equal after article strip.

name: only_one_side_has_series
why: Missing series metadata on one side is not evidence of a different book.

name: series_index_1_and_1_5_are_different_books
why: A #1.5 novella is not book 1. Indexes are compared as floats now, so 1 and 1.5 reject each other instead of truncating equal (issue #253).

name: title_near_miss_rejected_when_one_side_has_no_author
why: 'The Way of Kings' vs 'The Way of Kings Prime' scores 80. With no author to gate on the bar is 90, so these two different books no longer pair (issue #253).

name: missing_author_needs_a_high_title_score_to_pair
why: A missing author raises the bar to 90, it does not close the door: a 97 title score ('Assassins Apprentice' vs 'Assassin Apprentice') still pairs, with no author boost.

name: missing_author_rejects_a_mid_title_score
why: 85.7 clears the normal 75 threshold but not the 90 required when an author is missing - the case the raised bar exists for.

name: missing_author_on_the_ebook_side_raises_the_bar_too
why: The rule is symmetric: an author missing on either side raises the title bar to 90.

name: hash_exclusion_blocks_the_pair
why: A manual unpair recorded the audiobook's hash on the ebook - never re-pair.

name: hash_exclusion_recorded_on_the_audiobook_side
why: The exclusion is symmetric: either side's list blocks the pair.

name: id_exclusion_blocks_a_hashless_pair
why: The exclusion is keyed by row id as well as file hash now, so a hash-less row (legacy) keeps its memory of the unpair instead of re-pairing on the next scan (issue #253).

name: id_exclusion_names_a_different_book
why: The id list is matched against this candidate's id, not treated as a blanket block: an unpair from audiobook 22 must not stop audiobook 33 pairing.

name: different_authors_reject_a_perfect_title
why: Same title, different people - the author gate rejects before scoring.

name: same_series_different_index
why: Book 2 is not book 5, however similar the titles.

name: different_series_same_title
why: Series names below 85 are different series regardless of the title score.

name: title_near_miss_below_threshold
why: Two unrelated titles by the same author score under the threshold.

name: empty_titles_on_both_sides
why: Two empty titles are a perfect fuzzy match on nothing at all. Degenerate metadata is rejected outright now instead of scoring 100 (issue #253).

name: empty_title_on_one_side_only
why: An untitled row must not be paired with a real book on its author alone.

name: whitespace_only_title_is_empty_after_normalization
why: The empty-title rule is applied to the normalized title, so a title of blanks counts as empty too.
